mainTopic: Whether רבי ישמעאל is certain that an אנדרוגינוס is a בכור, and רב חסדא's view that a טומטום is a doubtful male or female
overview: In the משנה, רבי ישמעאל rules that a firstborn אנדרוגינוס (an animal with both male and female organs) may be slaughtered, because there is no greater מום than this. רבא asks whether רבי ישמעאל is sure that an אנדרוגינוס is a male בכור, or whether he is only unsure and means 'even if it is a בכור, it has a מום.' The גמרא explains that the answer matters for מלקות for shearing or working the animal, and for whether a כהן can demand it. A ברייתא of רבי אילעאי is brought as proof, but it is pushed off. A second ברייתא learns from an extra 'זכר' by the עולה that a טומטום and an אנדרוגינוס are excluded. The גמרא argues that this ברייתא must be רבי ישמעאל's, which would prove he was certain. That proof falls when the גמרא shows that the רבנן בתראי also have two 'זכר' words by בכור. Next, רב חסדא says the חכמים argue only about an אנדרוגינוס, while everyone agrees a טומטום is a doubtful male or female and is holy out of doubt. רבא challenges him: if so, a טומטום should be valued in ערכין.

steps.title: רבא asks what רבי ישמעאל's reasoning is
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks whether רבי ישמעאל is certain that an אנדרוגינוס is a בכור, or whether he is only speaking on the assumption that it might be one.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא asked: What is רבי ישמעאל's reason? Is it clear to him that an אנדרוגינוס is a בכור that comes with its blemish? Or maybe he is unsure, and he is speaking in an 'if you say' way: if you say it is a בכור, then it comes with its blemish.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא opens a question about רבי ישמעאל's ruling in the משנה. He gives two possible ways to understand it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both readings lead to the same result: the animal may be slaughtered because it has a מום. The difference is in the status itself. Either it is surely a בכור, or it is only a ספק בכור and the ruling is a 'just in case' argument.

keyTerms.meaning: He asks / raises a question he is unsure about
A creature with both male and female organs
Its blemish comes with it (it is born already blemished)
It is completely clear to him
He is truly unsure about it
If you should say: an argument that works even if the other side is right

steps.confusionAlert: Both sides agree that the animal may be slaughtered. רבא is not asking about the outcome. He is asking whether the animal surely has the status of a בכור.

phrases.aramaic: בָּעֵי רָבָא: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל?
phrases.english: Rava asked: What is the reason of Rabbi Yishmael?
phrases.notes: This is about רבי ישמעאל's ruling in our משנה: there's no greater blemish than this, so an אנדרוגינוס בכור may be slaughtered.

phrases.english: Is it completely obvious to him
that a hermaphrodite is a firstborn, and its blemish comes with it,
phrases.notes: The 'blemish' is its female organ, which it is born with.

phrases.english: or perhaps he is unsure about it,
and he is speaking in the manner of 'if you should say':
if you should say that it is a firstborn,
then its blemish is with it!

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי רָבָא: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens an investigation into the reasoning behind רבי ישמעאל's ruling in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי ישמעאל holds that an אנדרוגינוס is surely a בכור, or only possibly one.

steps.title: What difference does it make?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical difference there is between the two readings of רבי ישמעאל.
steps.whatsHappening: Since both readings permit slaughtering the animal, the גמרא asks why רבא's question matters. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A question in the גמרא needs a real result to be worth asking. Here the גמרא checks that רבא's question changes some practical law.

keyTerms.meaning: What practical difference comes out of it?

phrases.english: For what does it make a difference?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks why the question in step 1 matters in practice.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical result of choosing between 'certain' and 'unsure.'

steps.title: The difference: lashes, and giving it to the priest
steps.stepSummary: The difference is whether one gets מלקות for shearing or working the animal, and whether it must be given to a כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: The difference is for giving lashes for shearing it or working with it. Or also, for whether it must be given to a כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with two practical differences between the two readings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the animal is surely a בכור, then shearing it or working with it breaks a לאו, and the person gets מלקות. If it is only a ספק, he does not get מלקות. Also, if it is only a ספק, the כהן cannot force the owner to give it to him, because the one who wants to take from another must bring proof.

keyTerms.meaning: To give it to a כהן

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how a ספק status, unlike a certain status, changes both punishment and money matters.

phrases.english: For being lashed over it because of shearing and work,
or also, for giving it to a priest.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: מלקות for shearing or working the animal, and whether the כהן can demand it, depend on whether it is surely a בכור.

steps.title: Proof from רבי אילעאי's report of רבי ישמעאל
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא in which רבי אילעאי quotes רבי ישמעאל as saying flatly that an אנדרוגינוס is a בכור seems to show that he was certain.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבי אילעאי says in the name of רבי ישמעאל: An אנדרוגינוס is a בכור, and its blemish is with it. Learn from this that it is clear to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to answer רבא's question from a ברייתא. The ברייתא states רבי ישמעאל's view as a simple fact.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wording 'it is a בכור' sounds like a clear statement, not a doubt. So it seems רבי ישמעאל was certain.

phrases.english: Come and hear:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אִילְעַאי אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל:
phrases.english: Rabbi Ilai says in the name of Rabbi Yishmael:
A hermaphrodite is a firstborn, and its blemish is with it.
Learn from this that it is completely obvious to him!

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: רַבִּי אִילְעַאי אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to settle the question of step 1.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי ישמעאל is certain an אנדרוגינוס is a בכור.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא of רבי אילעאי quoting רבי ישמעאל in plain, definite wording.

steps.title: He may still mean 'if you say'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי ישמעאל's words in the ברייתא can still be read as an 'if you say' argument.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe he is speaking in the manner of 'if you should say'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes off the proof from step 4.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא does say plainly 'it is a בכור,' but even that wording could be a short way of saying 'even if it is a בכור, it has a מום.' So the proof does not settle רבא's question, and the גמרא looks for another source.

phrases.english: But perhaps he is speaking in the manner of 'if you should say'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 4.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole proof from רבי אילעאי's ברייתא.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The definite-sounding wording can still be read as a conditional 'if you say' argument.

steps.title: A new source: the extra 'male' in the burnt offering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that learns from the repeated word 'זכר' about the עולה that a טומטום and an אנדרוגינוס are excluded.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: 'A male', and not a female. When it says 'a male' below, which the verse did not need to say, why does the verse say it? To exclude a טומטום and an אנדרוגינוס.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up a second attempted proof from a ברייתא about the עולה. Steps 7–9 draw the inference about רבי ישמעאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first 'זכר' (ויקרא 1:3) already rules out a female. So the second 'זכר' (ויקרא 1:10) must teach something new: it rules out a טומטום and an אנדרוגינוס. The גמרא will use this extra exclusion to say something about the status of an אנדרוגינוס.

keyTerms.meaning: Why did the verse need to say it?
An animal whose organs are covered, so its gender is unknown

phrases.english: Come and hear: 'A male', and not a female.
When it says 'a male' below,
which the verse had no need to say,
why does the verse say it?
To exclude a tumtum and a hermaphrodite.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first proof was rejected, a new source is brought to try to settle רבא's question.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's question about the status of an אנדרוגינוס according to רבי ישמעאל (the inference comes next).
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא reading the extra 'זכר' about the עולה as excluding a טומטום and an אנדרוגינוס.

steps.title: Whose opinion is the ברייתא? Not the first תנא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whose view the ברייתא follows. It rejects the תנא קמא, because for him the אנדרוגינוס is only a doubt, and a פסוק would not be needed to exclude a doubt.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose opinion is this? If you say it is the first תנא, for him the אנדרוגינוס is a doubtful case. Would a פסוק come to exclude a doubtful case?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wants to use the ברייתא from Step 6 as a proof, so it first asks whose opinion the ברייתא follows. It tries the תנא קמא and rejects him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא of the משנה treats the אנדרוגינוס as a ספק, since we don't know if it is male or female. But a פסוק does not come to exclude a doubtful case: before Heaven there is no doubt, since the animal really is either male or female (רש״י). Since the ברייתא does use a פסוק to exclude the אנדרוגינוס, it cannot be following the תנא קמא.

keyTerms.meaning: The first, unnamed opinion in the משנה

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not whether an אנדרוגינוס may be brought as an עולה. Everyone agrees it may not. The question is why a פסוק would be needed to say so.

phrases.english: Whose opinion is this?
phrases.notes: He is asking about the ברייתא from Step 6, which used the repeated word 'זכר' by the עולה.

phrases.english: If you say it is the first תנא,
for him it is a doubtful case,
and would a verse come to exclude a doubtful case?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts working out the proof from the ברייתא brought in Step 6 by asking who its author is.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא of the משנה the ברייתא follows.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Not the תנא קמא, because a פסוק would not be needed to exclude a ספק.

steps.title: Not the latter Rabbis either, since they use only one verse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries the רבנן בתראי, but objects that by בכור they exclude all the cases from a single 'זכר'. The ברייתא, by contrast, uses two separate words.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps it is the latter Rabbis? But they learn everything from one verse. By בכור only one 'זכר' is written, and they exclude all of the cases from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a second possible author, the רבנן בתראי, and finds a problem with them too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן בתראי hold that an אנדרוגינוס is a separate kind of being, so a פסוק to exclude it would make sense for them. However, by בכור they use one 'זכר' to exclude a female, a טומטום, and an אנדרוגינוס all together. The ברייתא needs one 'זכר' for a female and a second one for a טומטום and an אנדרוגינוס, so it does not fit their method.

keyTerms.meaning: The 'latter Rabbis', the last opinion in the משנה
They derive it from one verse

phrases.english: Rather, it is the latter Rabbis?
But they derive it from one verse,
since regarding a firstborn
only one 'male' is written,
and they exclude all of them from it!
phrases.notes: The printed text has the word in round brackets; the corrected reading, in square brackets, adds 'and'. 'All of them' means the female, the טומטום and the אנדרוגינוס.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא רַבָּנַן בָּתְרָאֵי מֵחַד קְרָא נָפְקִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the תנא קמא is rejected, this tries the next candidate and rejects it too.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that the ברייתא follows the רבנן בתראי.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The רבנן בתראי exclude all three cases by בכור from one 'זכר', but the ברייתא uses two separate exclusions.

steps.title: It must be רבי ישמעאל, which proves he was certain
steps.stepSummary: Since the other two options failed, the ברייתא must follow רבי ישמעאל. A פסוק to exclude the אנדרוגינוס only makes sense if he was certain it is male, not just unsure.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is obviously רבי ישמעאל. If you say it was clear to רבי ישמעאל that an אנדרוגינוס is male, that is why a verse was needed to exclude it. But if you say he was unsure, would a verse be needed to exclude a doubtful case?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the proof begun in Step 6. The ברייתא must be רבי ישמעאל's, and that shows he held with certainty that an אנדרוגינוס is a בכור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי ישמעאל was sure the אנדרוגינוס is male, a פסוק to exclude it makes sense: רש״י explains it teaches that if it is set aside as an עולה, no holiness takes hold of it at all. If he was only unsure, then, as in Step 7, no פסוק would be needed. This would answer רבא's question from Step 1 about which reading of רבי ישמעאל is correct, but the next step pushes the proof away.

keyTerms.meaning: It is completely clear to him

phrases.english: Rather, it is obviously רבי ישמעאל,
and granted, if you say
that it is clear to רבי ישמעאל,
phrases.notes: He means it is clear that an אנדרוגינוס is a male בכור.

phrases.english: that is why a verse was needed to exclude it,
but if you say he is unsure about it,
would a verse be needed to exclude a doubtful case?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Having ruled out the other two candidates, it lands on רבי ישמעאל and draws the proof.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי ישמעאל held with certainty that an אנדרוגינוס is a בכור.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא that uses a second 'זכר' by עולה to exclude the טומטום and the אנדרוגינוס, which only makes sense if the author saw the אנדרוגינוס as definitely male.

steps.title: Really the latter Rabbis, since בכור also has two verses
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. The ברייתא can follow the רבנן בתראי after all, because by בכור there are also two פסוקים, 'הזכר' and 'הזכרים'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Actually, it is the latter Rabbis. Regarding a firstborn, two verses are written: 'the male' and 'the males'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the proof from Step 9 by removing the objection from Step 8.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8 assumed that by בכור the רבנן בתראי had only one 'זכר'. In fact there are two, so their method matches the ברייתא: one word excludes a female, and the other excludes a טומטום and an אנדרוגינוס. The ברייתא therefore proves nothing about רבי ישמעאל, and the question of whether he was certain stays open.

keyTerms.meaning: Actually; really (returning to an option that was rejected)

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא about עולה does not prove that רבי ישמעאל was certain. It fits the רבנן בתראי, who have two 'זכר' words by בכור as well.

phrases.english: Actually, it is the latter Rabbis,
and regarding a firstborn, two verses are written:
'The male' and 'the males'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Undoes the proof of Step 9 by answering the objection from Step 8.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole proof that the ברייתא must be רבי ישמעאל's.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed that בכור has only one 'זכר'. In fact there are two, so the רבנן בתראי fit the ברייתא.

steps.title: The argument is only about the hermaphrodite
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the חכמים in the משנה. רב חסדא says their argument with רבי ישמעאל is only about an אנדרוגינוס. By a טומטום, all agree it is a doubt and is holy because of the doubt.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And the חכמים say: it is not a בכור, etc.' רב חסדא said: The argument is about an אנדרוגינוס. But about a טומטום, everyone agrees it is a doubt, and it is holy because of the doubt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new section by quoting the חכמים from the משנה. רב חסדא then explains exactly which case they are arguing about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אנדרוגינוס has both male and female parts, so the חכמים can treat it as its own kind of creature, and therefore not a בכור. A טומטום is different, because it really is either male or female; we just can't see which. So even the חכמים agree it might be a male בכור, and it gets holiness out of doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: One whose private parts are covered, so we can't tell if it is male or female

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רב חסדא is saying the חכמים agree with רבי ישמעאל completely. They still argue about the אנדרוגינוס; they only agree about the טומטום.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the key idea that a טומטום is a 'hidden male or female.' רבא is about to challenge exactly that idea.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say: It is not a firstborn, etc.
Rav Chisda said:
The dispute is regarding a hermaphrodite,
but regarding a tumtum,
everyone agrees it is an uncertain case,
and it is holy because of the doubt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new section by going back to the חכמים's words in the משנה, after the ברייתא discussion in steps 6-10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מחלוקת between רבי ישמעאל and the חכמים is only about an אנדרוגינוס. A טומטום is agreed by all to be a doubtful male or female, so it is holy out of doubt.

steps.title: Then a טומטום should be valued in ערכין
steps.stepSummary: רבא challenges רב חסדא. If a טומטום is surely either male or female, then when someone pledges its ערך, it should be valued.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: If so, then by ערכין, a טומטום should be able to be valued!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks רב חסדא's idea that a טומטום is just a hidden male or female. He points out where that idea would lead in the laws of ערכין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ערך of a person is a fixed amount that depends on being male or female. If a טומטום is really one or the other, it should get a ערך, at least as a doubt. רבא assumes this does not happen, so he concludes that רב חסדא's view of the טומטום seems wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: If that is so, then...: introduces a problem that follows from what was just said
Valuations: pledging to give the Torah's fixed value of a person to the בית המקדש

phrases.english: Rava said to him:
If that is so,
phrases.notes: He means: if a טומטום is really either male or female, just hidden.

phrases.english: regarding valuations, it should be valued?
phrases.notes: רבא says this as a surprise. He is assuming everyone knows a טומטום does not get a ערך.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly challenges רב חסדא's statement in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's claim that a טומטום is, by everyone's view, a doubtful male or female.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a טומטום is surely male or female, it should follow that it can be valued in ערכין, where value depends on being male or female. Since it is not valued, it seems a טומטום is not simply a hidden male or female.
